description.value: A voxel-based morphometry study examined grey matter volume differences between abstinent cocaine-dependent individuals and healthy controls, including sex-specific group comparisons.

spans.text: This study examined sex-related differences in grey matter volume between cocaine-dependent and healthy control subjects using voxel-based morphometry.

Thirty-six voluntary treatment-seeking individuals (18 men/18 women; ages 25–46) who met DSM-IV Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition (DSM-IV) criteria for current cocaine dependence were admitted to the Clinical Neuroscience Research Unit of the Connecticut Mental Health Center for 4 weeks of inpatient treatment for cocaine dependence and research participation.
Fifty healthy comparison subjects (28 men/22 women; ages 18–50) were also recruited from the community through local advertisements.
